newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NCC Siab merger seen sound.
newsitem.headline: NCC Siab merger seen sound.

text.p: The merger between Swedish building and real estate companies NCC and SIAB, announced on Tuesday, was a sensible move which will improve product mix, analysts said.
"The deal is strategically sound," an analyst said. "A larger player is needed to meet competition."
"I think the product mix in the new company will be strong. NCC has been too focused on the construction area, but with the merger that part is decreasing in relation to the business area housing."
The merged company will have a turnover of 34.8 billion crowns and the largest business area will be housing with sales of 28 billion crowns, followed by construction with 10 billion crowns.
But on the negative side, analysts questioned company estimates of annual synergies of 200-300 million crowns and said Siab's real estate holdings were weak.
"The synergies are poorly detailed; it is hard to say where they will be made...This raises the operating margin by 0.7-1.0 percent which is a lot in the construction sector," an analyst said.
Analysts were not, however, worried about the companies not intending to spin-off real estate holdings, despite Siab being weak in this segment.
The merged company will have real estate holdings, scattered around the country, worth more than 17 billion crowns.
"They will continue to concentrate the holdings and restructure, which is a positive development," an analyst said.
"Something needs to be done, maybe a spin-off, but the question is what such a real estate company would be worth."
Another analyst thinks the market might force the merged company to spin off its real estate holdings.
"I do not think NCC wants to spin off its real estate...But it might have to. The market and NCC's advisors will almost demand it to increase the value of the company," an analyst said.
